changes.before: Confirmed as of 2026-09-23: the 180-day moratorium (Ordinance 2025-28) expired on its own terms around 2026-06-13. Independent reporting from The Ohio Newsroom/Statehouse News Bureau (2026-02-26) and Scioto Post (2026-03) both describe South Bloomfield as having 'preemptively eliminat[ed] all areas of industrial zoning, in order to avoid applications from data centers,' corroborating the row's existing 'outcome' (new 2025 zoning book that does not list data centers as a permitted use). No extension or replacement moratorium was found; the village's approach has moved from a temporary pause to eliminating the zoning category itself.
changes.after: Signed Ordinance 2026-06 records May 18, 2026 passage and imposes a new 180-day data-center application/permit pause while its recital describes extending Ordinance 2025-28. It permits early rescission or extension; immediate effect is conditional on the required Council votes. Identity/continuity between the acts, actual effectiveness, operative interval, later action and the legacy replacement classification remain unresolved. [VERIFY: instrument relationship, operative interval, later amendments/extensions/repeal, judicial developments and current legal force.]
changes.reason: Signed Ordinance 2026-06 contradicts the prior statement that no extension or replacement moratorium was found.
